Legend

Condensation-favorability index 0-100 (DERIVED from HRRR analysis, fixed absolute scale): 0 No condensation tan (dew-point depression at/above 2.5 C with RH at/below 60%) → 20 Relative humidity gold → 40 Dew-point depression green → 60 Dew-point depression teal → 80 Surfaces stay wet steel blue → 100 Saturation deep blue (spread at/below 0 C with RH 100%). Relative humidity alone reaches 35; the depression term alone reaches 65; both together reach saturation. Same index always shows the same color — not relative humidity renamed, not dew point renamed, no fog visibility gate.

A derived condensation-favorability index from operational HRRR temperature, dew point, and humidity analysis: where near-surface air sits closest to saturation, dew, frost, and moisture films form on boats, docks, optics, and shoreline surfaces. High values flag nights and mornings when surfaces stay wet. Derivation: condensation = 100*(0.65*clip((2.5-S)/2.5,0,1)^0.7 + 0.35*clip((RH-60)/40,0,1)), S = TMP-DPT in C deg. Answers how close near-surface air is to saturation (dew/frost/film condensation potential). Uses no wind or visibility data, unlike fog risk; is not relative humidity or dew point itself.

Condensation science (surface thermodynamics and boundary-layer meteorology) studies the phase change when humid air contacts surfaces at or below the dew point. The dew-point depression (temperature minus dew point) measures the remaining cooling needed; relative humidity weights how broadly saturated the air mass is. Together they predict dew and frost formation relevant to agriculture, infrastructure, and Great Lakes marine operations.

Units: condensation index 0-100 (display; derived, see derivation)
